name: The Bended Elbow
description: A contemporary Australian styled hotel on Dean Street spread over two levels with multiple dining areas. There is a rooftop beer garden, a Melbourne-style alfresco laneway and a modern bistro, with a bar pouring tap beers, wines, spirits and cocktails. The venue runs live music and trivia nights and takes private function bookings.
highlights: Rooftop beer garden open Thursday to Saturday
Two-level venue with several dining areas
Tap beers, wines, spirits and cocktails

name: Sodens Hotel
description: A Wilson Street hotel with a family-friendly bistro, a sports bar and a beer garden. It has TAB, Keno and gaming facilities and a kids' play area, and runs live music on Friday and Saturday nights. Private function spaces include the Stable Bar, the Lounge and the Birdcage, used for birthdays, Christmas parties, business events, weddings and wakes.
highlights: Beer garden and kids' play area
Three function spaces: Stable Bar, Lounge and Birdcage

name: Commercial Club Albury
description: A large licensed club on Dean Street. Dining is spread across The Grill restaurant and Reflections Cafe, which serves breakfast and pastries from the club's own bakehouse, and there is a sports bar beside The Grill with multiple screens for sport and racing, TAB and Keno and an outdoor courtyard. The club also runs gaming promotions, artist shows and bands, a bottle shop, an on-site golf motel and sporting sections covering golf, lawn bowls, cue sports, squash and gym.
highlights: The Grill restaurant and Reflections Cafe
Sports bar with TAB, Keno and outdoor courtyard
Function rooms from board meetings to large events
Golf, lawn bowls, cue sports, squash and gym sections

name: SS&A Albury
description: The Albury Sailors, Soldiers and Airmen's Club on Olive Street, which traces its origins to a 1944 war services hall appeal. It has three bars with distinct identities: The Studio with free live entertainment on Friday and Saturday nights, the Aurum Lounge, and The Locker Room sports bar with giant screens and betting facilities. There is also a cafe and the Social Bar and Dining restaurant serving club and pub classics such as steaks, schnitzels and burgers alongside Asian dishes and a kids' menu, plus conference and function facilities and free on-site parking.
highlights: Three bars: The Studio, Aurum Lounge and The Locker Room
Free live entertainment Friday and Saturday nights
Sports bar with giant screens and betting facilities
Social Bar and Dining restaurant plus a cafe
Free on-site parking, wheelchair access via David Street

name: Albion Hotel
description: A Dean Street pub that has been part of the Albury CBD for over 100 years. The ground floor bistro serves pub-style counter meals and there is a rooftop bar upstairs for cocktails, spritzes and a grazing menu. The hotel also operates three function rooms and runs a bottomless brunch on Saturdays and Sundays.
highlights: Ground floor bistro with pub-style counter meals
Rooftop bar with cocktails and grazing menu

name: Public House Albury
description: A Dean Street pub serving contemporary pub food built on locally grown seasonal produce, alongside craft beers, regional wines and an extensive cocktail list that includes pre-order Cocktail Trees of twelve cocktails and frozen Poptails. Weekly regulars include happy hour from 4pm to 6pm daily, mini martinis on Wednesday evenings, two-for-one pizzas from noon on Thursdays and DJs from 9pm on Friday and Saturday. A kids menu is available and the venue takes function bookings.
highlights: Contemporary pub food from local seasonal produce
Craft beers, regional wines and an extensive cocktail list

name: Beer Deluxe Albury
description: A Kiewa Street pub that describes itself as Albury's home of entertainment, good times and cold beers. It has a beer garden, large screens showing live sport, a pub classics kitchen and a stage used for live music and touring acts. Trivia nights and function bookings are also offered.

name: Star Hotel
description: A Guinea Street hotel established in 1874 with a newly renovated public bar, a bistro, a sports bar and a beer garden. Carlton Draught tank beer is poured on site. Two function spaces, The Laneway and The Shed, are available for events.
highlights: Renovated public bar and sports bar
The Laneway and The Shed function spaces

name: Astor Hotel Albury
description: A Young Street hotel that describes its look as where retro meets modern. It combines a pub and bar with a food offering the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide describes as pub style meals featuring a woodfire grill and rotisserie. The hotel also has accommodation, hosts live events and is used as a function and photoshoot venue.
highlights: Retro-styled hotel bar and dining room
Pub meals from a woodfire grill and rotisserie

name: Brady's Railway Hotel
description: A Smollett Street pub with a bistro serving pub food and contemporary Australian dishes, a beer garden, and a public bar showing live sport. There is a drive-through bottle shop open until midnight Monday to Saturday. Weekly regulars include raffles, trivia, music bingo, joker poker and a members draw, and the hotel has function facilities.
highlights: Bistro open for lunch daily and dinner nightly
Raffles, trivia, music bingo and joker poker

name: Dux Albury
description: A Dean Street bar and dining room offering curated wines, cocktails and share plates, with bar seating and intimate dining. Private event bookings can be made outside standard trading hours. Dux was named a Critics' Pick in the SMH Good Food Guide 2025.
highlights: Private event bookings outside standard hours
Critics' Pick, SMH Good Food Guide 2025

name: The Thirsty Devil Brewery
description: A micro brewery on Townsend Street that brews on site and pours from a 14-tap bar. There are two beer gardens, a large function room and the Hungry Devil food van operating during peak times. The bar also serves cocktails such as espresso martinis, Aperol spritzes and ginger mules and produces its own spirits. Dogs are welcome on leads and live music runs seasonally in the warmer months.
highlights: Hungry Devil food van at peak times
Seasonal live music in the warmer months

name: Boomerang Hotel
description: A Wagga Road hotel in Lavington with a family bistro serving pub fare, steaks and kids meals, a sports bar with TAB, and gaming facilities. Breakfast is served daily from 7.30am. The hotel has 38 motel rooms with ensuites, air-conditioning, TV and WiFi, an indoor pool, and function rooms used for birthdays, weddings and corporate events.
highlights: Family bistro with steaks and a kids menu

name: Kinross Woolshed
description: A hotel in Thurgoona set in a converted woolshed on a wide open site. It has a sports bar, a bistro, a beer garden and outdoor deck, and a gaming lounge, plus function spaces. The venue hosts live music and entertainment and is family friendly.

name: Jindera Hotel
description: A country pub in the centre of Jindera serving classic pub meals and drinks. It offers indoor and outdoor dining with a spacious beer garden and runs regular community events. Disabled access is available.
highlights: Country pub in the centre of Jindera

name: Howlong Golf Resort
description: A golf club and resort on Golf Club Drive at Howlong. Alongside the golf course it runs the Fairways Bistro, a pro shop, on-site resort accommodation and a functions venue. Separate contact lines are published for the pro shop, accommodation, bistro and memberships.

name: Club Corowa
description: The Corowa RSL club on Betterment Parade, trading as Club Corowa. It has a bistro and cafe with alfresco dining, a club lounge and the Silks sports bar serving cocktails, gourmet pizza and appetisers. Function spaces run across three levels and include a high-tech auditorium. The club also has indoor and outdoor playgrounds and an 18-hole Mini Golf on the Murray course, and runs a shuttle service from Thursday to Sunday between 5pm and close.
highlights: Bistro and cafe with alfresco dining
Function spaces across three levels plus an auditorium
Shuttle service Thursday to Sunday from 5pm

name: Wodonga RSL
description: An RSL club on Reid Street with The Fowlers Stove Bistro, which seats 100 inside plus an alfresco balcony, and a bar stocking local wines and Australian beverages. The club is pokie free and family friendly, welcoming veterans, families and the general public. Function rooms are available for hire and a courtesy bus runs Friday nights from 5pm to 9pm across local suburbs for a gold coin donation.
highlights: The Fowlers Stove Bistro, 100 seats plus alfresco balcony
Open on ANZAC Day and Remembrance Day

name: Blazing Stump Hotel
description: A family pub and dining venue on Anzac Parade that has operated on the site since 1880. It has a modern sports bar with the biggest sports screen in Wodonga, a large outdoor tank bar deck pouring brewery-fresh tank beer, a bottle shop open until late, and a 400 seat bistro that includes a Mountain deck looking out to the ranges.
highlights: Modern sports bar with the biggest sports screen in Wodonga
Outdoor tank bar deck with tank beer on tap

name: Huon Hill Hotel
description: A Reid Street pub and bistro in Wodonga. The bistro menu blends classic pub favourites with pizzas, gourmet burgers, salads and pub-style mains, and the venue publishes daily bistro specials and a live music line-up on its What's On page. Function bookings are taken and table bookings can be made online.
highlights: Bistro with pizzas, gourmet burgers, salads and pub mains

name: Church St Hotel
description: A hotel on Church Street in central Wodonga described in the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide as a gastro pub serving contemporary cuisine and cocktails. The hotel's own site lists food and drink service, accommodation bookings, function facilities and special events.

name: The Lincoln
description: A gastro pub on Gateway Island at Wodonga, described in the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide as having a cocktail lounge and beer garden. The venue serves casual bistro dining and offers large flexible indoor and outdoor spaces used for corporate functions, private events and weddings. Online bookings and gift cards are available.
highlights: Large indoor and outdoor function spaces

name: The Goods Shed
description: A bar and restaurant on Church Street, Wodonga running a seasonal menu and what it calls the largest craft beer fridge between Melbourne and Sydney. Pizza and fries are served daily between 3pm and 5pm. The venue takes online reservations and function bookings and sells gift vouchers.

name: Wodonga Golf Club
description: A golf club on Clubhouse Place set in a natural bush environment where native trees are a feature and Felltimber Creek runs through the layout. The course measures over 6,100 metres and is open daily except Christmas Day. On site are the Clubhouse Bar & Bistro, open Wednesday to Sunday for lunch and dinner with Sunday lunch, a lounge and spike bar, the only golf shop in Wodonga, and function and corporate event spaces.
highlights: Course over 6,100 metres in a bush setting
Felltimber Creek runs through the course
Clubhouse Bar & Bistro open Wednesday to Sunday

name: The Birallee Tavern
description: A locally owned tavern on Melrose Drive in Wodonga serving meals and drinks for occasions from casual lunches to celebrations. The venue has a dining room, a deck seating area, Bobby's Bar for cocktails and the Bira Bar gaming room, and hosts functions and events.

name: Tanswell's Hotel
description: A hotel built in 1853 on Ford Street in the centre of Beechworth. It has a front bar, a bandroom used for live music, and two levels of different dining areas. The kitchen serves lunch from noon to 2pm and dinner from 5.30pm to 8.30pm seven days, and the hotel takes accommodation and function bookings.
highlights: Built in 1853 in the centre of Beechworth

name: Bridge Road Brewers
description: A brewery and taproom on Ford Street, Beechworth, with a second venue in Brunswick East and an outlet at Melbourne Airport. The Beechworth venue serves pizza alongside the brewery's beers, sells packaged beer to take away, and runs tastings, events and venue bookings.
highlights: Pizza served with the beer range

name: Star Hotel Yackandandah
description: A High Street pub first opened in 1863 and bought by Matt and Kim Frauenfelder in 2016, since restored with a renovated restaurant and beer garden. The kitchen centres on a fusion of southern USA and Australian barbecue with all meat smoked on the premises in hand-made smokers. The bar pours local beer through a partnership with Two Pot Brewing Co, gin and spirits from Yack Creek and Backwoods distilleries, and local wines and ciders. The pub is a live music venue and hosts a main stage for the Yackandandah Folk Festival and the Spring Migration Festival.
highlights: Local beer from Two Pot Brewing Co
Gin and spirits from Yack Creek and Backwoods distilleries
Live music venue and festival stage

name: Telegraph Hotel
description: A hotel on Conness Street in the middle of Chiltern's historic streetscape. The bistro serves parmigiana, pizzas, fish and chips, steaks and burgers, and the pub has a large beer garden and TAB. Friday nights bring community raffles, and happy hours run through the week.
highlights: In Chiltern's historic Conness Street streetscape
Bistro with parmigiana, pizza, steaks and burgers

name: The Victoria Hotel Rutherglen
description: A landmark heritage hotel on Rutherglen's Main Street redeveloped as an owner-operated boutique hotel, and awarded AHA Victoria's Best Redeveloped Hotel. The restaurant serves flame-focused cooking with an emphasis on local produce and lunch and dinner run seven days, with takeaway pizza also available. Accommodation is 14 king suites, some of them dog friendly, and there are event spaces for functions.
highlights: Heritage hotel on Rutherglen's Main Street
14 boutique king suites, select rooms dog friendly
